challenge.better_approach: I looked at filling owners mechanically from each ticket's bounds.in or decisions writes_to. Measured on 94e1: that gives feedback's charter, which is wrong, because the ticket settled a decision record. Reading each ticket is the price, and the orchestrator named it.
challenge.hidden_assumption: That every PROVED ticket has one charter owner. Measured: 94e1 does not have a charter as its owner. The ticket therefore allows a recorded no-charter finding, which is a question for Akien if the store needs a value.
challenge.prior_art: The cast door (cairn/tools/base/transitions.py:2227) already requires owning_intention on new casts, so the 100 are legacy. 3ca32dd07e86's fill (data_recorder, read first, pair invented 0.036) is the worked example. The memory 'backfill writes beside without reading' is the failure mode this ticket guards against.
challenge.real_collision: None. A separate measurement found 44 PROVED tickets whose owner path does not resolve by a naive check. That is a different defect, recorded here and not in scope.

answers.falsifier: Over the live commons, no PROVED ticket's owning_intention is blank; each filled owner resolves to a charter on disk; and each fill's journal line carries a why naming what was read. A fill written from the title alone (94e1's title says feedback, while its read found it settled a decision) is the failure.
answers.from_idea: none, because the orchestrator ruled the shape 2026-11-16 from the measurement that 100 of 813 PROVED tickets under CairnCommons/tickets/ carry a blank owning_intention (3ca32dd07e86 and 94e1cce8941e among them)
answers.how: For each blank PROVED ticket: read its intention, how, falsifier and the files its build wrote, and name the charter whose claim it proved. Write it through cairn artifact write, one ticket at a time, recording the read in the why. A ticket whose read finds no charter owner (it settled a decision, or its component is gone) gets that finding, not a guess. A proof under cairn/tools/base/proofs/ holds over the live commons that no PROVED ticket's owning_intention is blank.
answers.traces_to: Law 6 (everything has exactly one owner) and Law 3 (nothing is known until measured): intention_fidelity cannot pair a charter with a ticket whose owner is blank, so those charters read as never proved.
answers.what: Every PROVED ticket names its owning_intention, and each of the 100 blank ones is read before its owner is filled.

bullets.text: 100 of 813 PROVED tickets name no owner, so intention_fidelity cannot see what they proved; the fill reads each one first.
